slot.brief: Given the rms electric field of an EM wave, compute the average energy density using u = ε₀E².

stem: In vacuum, an electromagnetic wave has an rms electric field of $200$ V m$^{-1}$. Taking $\text{ε}_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ F m$^{-1}$, its average energy density is:

verdicts.working: For an electromagnetic wave, the average total energy density is \(u=\varepsilon_0 E_{\rm rms}^2\). Thus \(u=(8.85\times10^{-12})(200)^2=3.54\times10^{-7}\,\text{J m}^{-3}\).

working:
$u=\text{ε}_0 E_{\rm rms}^2$\n$u=(8.85\times10^{-12})(200)^2=3.54\times10^{-7}$ J m$^{-3}$

Independent check: For an electromagnetic wave, the average total energy density is \(u=\varepsilon_0 E_{\rm rms}^2\). Thus \(u=(8.85\times10^{-12})(200)^2=3.54\times10^{-7}\,\text{J m}^{-3}\).
solution:
For an electromagnetic wave, the average total energy density is $u=\varepsilon_0 E_{\rm rms}^2$.
$$u=(8.85\times10^{-12})(200)^2=3.54\times10^{-7}\ \text{J m}^{-3}$$
